newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Happy times are here again for Brussels bourse.
newsitem.headline: Happy times are here again for Brussels bourse.

text.p: Sentiment, the dollar, interest rates and the general absence of bad news combined to push the Brussels bourse to new highs in early trading on Friday, with no near end in sight to the rally, traders said.
"There is no real excitement, but the general tone is very positive," one trader said. "There is a lack of bad news, the dollar is strong and interest rates are low and, in some areas, easing."
The Bel-20 index of blue chip shares was 12.08 points or 0.53 percent higher at 2,295.15 at 0900 GMT, having earlier hit a new intra-day high of 2,297.87.
The main feature of the market, and a strong influence on the overall index, was non-ferrous metals group Union Miniere, up 3.25 percent to 3,180 francs in a volume of some 26,000 shares.

Traders said the rise, building on strong positive movements earlier in the week, was due to a combination of the strong dollar and zinc prices -- both of which have a major influence on the company's bottom line.
There is also the prospect of the company getting more involved in copper and cobalt in the Democratic Republic of Congo -- formerly Zaire.
Chief Executive Officer Karel Vinck visited the country last month after the revolution that ousted President Mobutu Sese Seko.
"There is a very positive and growing feeling for Union Miniere. People are starting to think of the good old days when its share price was an indicator of the state of the country," one trader said.
The market was also lifted by a flurry of basket buying, particularly involving chemical firm Solvay whose shares are to be split 10 for one. The stock was 1.1 percent up at 22,050 francs.
